I am a Ph.D. candidate in the [Department of Statistics](https://www.stat.iastate.edu/) at [Iowa State University](https://www.iastate.edu/), advised by [Professor Jae Kwang Kim](https://sites.google.com/view/jaekwangkim/home) and [Professor Chunlin Li](https://statistics.as.virginia.edu/people/chunlin-li). I expect to complete my Ph.D. in May 2027.

My research focuses on calibration weighting, missing data, data integration, and high-dimensional mediation analysis. I combine statistical theory, computation, and collaborative data analysis to develop methods for biomedical and population survey data.

I am a graduate research assistant at Iowa State’s [Center for Survey Statistics and Methodology](https://www.cssm.iastate.edu/). My applied experience includes integrating survey and remote-sensing data for the National Resources Inventory. Before joining Iowa State, I served as a lecturer in statistics at [Jagannath University](https://jnu.ac.bd/) and [BAIUST](https://baiust.ac.bd/) in Bangladesh.

## Research interests

- **Statistical methods:** Calibration and balancing weights, missing data, data integration, causal inference, high-dimensional mediation, and adaptive sampling.
- **Applications:** Molecular and proteomics data, biomedical and population health research, and survey–remote sensing integration.

My current work studies reliable inference with partially observed data, shared molecular contributions across multiple outcomes, and efficient allocation of costly measurements. [Read more about my research](research.qmd).
